statement: The application shall let users search for a title or browse by genre.
The application shall return results from multiple sites in one place.
The application shall let users filter the source types they want to see.
The application shall present results in a clean, organized view for comparison.
The application shall let users save favorites and manage the favorites list later.
The application shall allow users to return to useful sources without searching again.
The system shall support end users.
The system shall support system maintainers.
The system shall allow system maintainers to control which external sites are included in searches.
The system shall provide system maintainers with visibility into whether external sources are working well.
The system shall provide maintainers with notification when a source stops responding.
The system shall provide maintainers with notification when a source starts timing out.
The system shall provide maintainers with notification when a source returns broken results.
The system shall provide maintainers with notification when a source returns empty results.
The system shall track source response time as a performance indicator.
The system shall track the last successful crawl or check for each source.
The system shall provide a dashboard showing each source's current status.
The system shall provide a dashboard showing each source's last check time.
The system shall provide a dashboard showing recent failures for each source.
The system shall alert maintainers when a source is down for more than a short period.
The system shall alert maintainers when a source is failing repeatedly.
The system shall use a simple threshold-based approach to assess source reliability.
Repeated failures or consistently poor response times shall move a source into a warning state and then into a disabled state if the problems continue.
If a source is only flaky, the system may still show it in search results but rank it lower or flag it for maintainers.
If a source is clearly down, the system shall temporarily exclude it from searches until it recovers.
The exact reliability thresholds shall be agreed with the team.
The video search should work across multiple sites.
Users should be able to do the needed actions with the search results.
Maintainers should have controls over the sources.

The application needs to support filtering.

The system shall provide administrators with a straightforward way to enable or disable external sites without touching code.
Users should be able to choose whether they want streaming sources, downloadable listings, or both when narrowing down a search.
The initial version shall include the core functions that were described as needed.
The system should display the source site for each result.
The system should perform basic relevance sorting so the best matches appear first.
When a source is down or times out, the search shall still return whatever results it can from the other sources.
The interface should provide simple toggles or checkboxes near the search box for selecting streaming sources, downloadable listings, or both.
The selection controls should be obvious and quick to change before running a search.
Each search result shall display the title.
Each search result shall indicate whether it is streaming or downloadable.

The system should provide basic search history.

The system should support organizing favorites if possible.

Users shall be able to search across multiple video sources from one place.
The system shall present search results in a clean and organized way.

The system shall allow management of which external sites are included in search coverage.
The system shall make the search experience feel simple and trustworthy.
The system shall allow users to compare options without jumping around or getting lost in clutter.
The system shall allow users to save useful results as favorites so they can return to them later.
The system shall support multiple external sites cleanly.
The system shall enable users to find what they are looking for faster than they do today.
The system shall track search completion rate as a relevant metric.
The system shall support at least two main user groups.
The system shall allow regular end users to filter by source type.
The system shall support three main stakeholder roles: end users, maintainers, and the person overseeing the product or operations.

The system shall support searching for a title or genre.
The system shall provide a high-level view of usage and quality.
The system shall report whether users are saving favorites or returning to the system.
If a source times out or is down, the system shall keep the rest of the search running instead of failing the whole query.
If data comes back incomplete or inconsistent, the system shall still present what it can.
The system shall support scheduled engagement on a recurring basis rather than constant engagement.
A timeout shall be treated as a partial failure.
For inconsistent or incomplete data, the system shall avoid presenting the data as authoritative.
Questionable data shall be kept only while it remains useful.
Cached results may be retained for a short time to keep searches fast.
If a source keeps failing or returning poor data, the system shall automatically stop relying on that source after some threshold, at least temporarily.
The system shall avoid misrepresenting content rights.
The system shall minimize data related to searches and favorites when tracking them.
The system shall handle data in accordance with applicable policy or compliance rules.
The system shall follow the usual copyright obligations for the regions in which the business operates.
The system shall follow the usual privacy obligations for the regions in which the business operates.
If there are specific rules around linking to streams, those rules shall shape what the system stores.
If there are specific rules around linking to streams, those rules shall shape what the system displays.
If there are specific rules around linking to streams or handling user data, those rules shall shape how much detail the system keeps in logs.

The system shall avoid displaying anything that appears to republish the content or add extra rights claims on top of it.

The system shall enforce clear retention limits for favorites and search history.

The system shall not exclude a source too quickly based on one bad run.
The system shall trigger action fairly fast after repeated failures.
The threshold and cooldown behavior shall be configurable.
The system shall avoid spending too much time or capacity retrying known-bad sources.
The system shall avoid slowing down the whole search experience by retrying known-bad sources.
The system should prioritize protecting overall search performance.
The system shall alert maintainers when a source crosses the failure threshold.
The system shall support email for routine notifications.
The system shall also surface alerts in the team’s operational dashboard or incident channel when a source starts impacting search quality.
The system shall automatically reduce the priority of an external source when it repeatedly fails or provides poor data.
If failures continue after priority reduction, the system shall temporarily disable the external source to prevent it from hurting search quality.
Maintainers shall be able to manually override the disabled state of an external source.
Maintainers should not need to manage every external source during normal operation.
The system shall provide a dashboard summary for the normal view.
The system shall send direct notifications only when a source crosses a meaningful threshold or is disabled.
The system shall provide a periodic report showing trends over time.

The interface shall work well with screen readers.
Search and filtering shall not depend on mouse-only interactions.

The interface shall provide readable contrast.

The app shall provide a lightweight first-time walkthrough.

The first-time walkthrough or contextual tips shall be skippable.

The app shall provide a searchable FAQ.

The system shall keep important details consistent.

The system shall test each site integration individually.
The system shall monitor failures and slow responses.
The system shall have onboarding and help content ready at launch.
The system shall support a phased rollout.
The initial rollout shall start with a small internal or pilot user group before the system is opened up broadly.
The rollout shall target users who are comfortable giving early feedback.
The system shall use feedback from early users to assess whether search results are understandable before full launch.
The migration process shall help users switch from checking multiple sites separately to using one place first.
The system shall make search results trustworthy and familiar to users right away.
The system shall provide enough detail for users to verify search results against the sites they already know.
The migration process shall map old source lists into the new control process.
The system shall enable favorites after the core search has been released.
The system shall enable less critical sources in stages once the basics are stable.
The system shall avoid exposing users to unfinished parts of the workflow all at once.
Early users shall include a small mix of power users and practical testers from the target audience.
Early users shall be people who already search across multiple sites and are willing to report what feels confusing or missing.
The migration should be a gradual shift in which the new platform runs alongside the old approach at first.
Users should be able to try the new platform without being forced to change overnight.
Search results should be complete enough for users to feel confident in the system.
Filters should behave predictably for users.
Saved favorites should not be lost during migration.
If a source or feature must be paused, the system should communicate this clearly so it still feels dependable.
The system should make the transfer feel as invisible as possible.
When replacing an older tool, the system should automatically carry over favorites.
If something cannot migrate cleanly, the system should clearly say so and let the user re-save it instead of losing it silently.
The system should provide a short in-product message or walkthrough explaining what changed.
The system should keep old searches or source links available for a while as a fallback.
The system shall introduce the new search experience to a limited group first as a staged transition.
The system shall compare the new search experience against the old workflow during the transition.
The system shall widen access only after the results and source coverage are reliable.
The system shall provide users with simple guidance.
The system shall preserve users' favorites if possible.
The system shall display clear notices when a result comes from a different site than the user expected.
The system shall monitor performance issues so the platform remains stable while users are moving over.
